messages:
Maria: heads-up — we start tenant-reshard backfill tomorrow 03:00 UTC. main risk: dashboards hitting stale route keys and causing long-running console queries.

Sam: do we have an estimate for how many console queries will touch the hottest partitions during the backfill window?

Maria: rough estimate: ~120k reads/hr for route-profile joins. without a read-adapter p99 could climb to ~5s. recommend canary first.

Devon: +1 for canary. Proposed flow: dual-write route_key_v2, enable read-adapter that prefers v2 with v1 fallback. Backfill will be rate-limited and tenant-scoped.

Lee: important question — how will quota routing behave? quota subsystem currently derives buckets from route_key_v1.

Maria: quota-proxy will use a temporary alias mapping (route_key_alias). We'll add a lookup layer: SELECT quota_bucket FROM route_key_alias WHERE v2_key = $1; fallback to v1.

Arjun: aliasing could increase cardinality transiently. concerned about index bloat on quota-dedicated tables.

Maria: mitigation: TTL on alias rows at 30d, coalesce duplicates during backfill, and emit alias_cardinality metric. Alert if >25% above baseline.

Sam: dashboards cache inconsistency is my worry — mixed reads could show different numbers on the same panel.

Devon: UI mitigation: (a) soft-toggle to read from v2 for X% of sessions, (b) show a freshness badge when data is mixed, (c) daily reconcile job that flags panels with >2% drift.

Lee: ops would prefer a silent migration. can we avoid adding badges for most tenants?

Maria: we can run silent for 90% of tenants and enable badge for 10% canary cohort to capture UX regressions.

Console-bot: deploy scheduled: dualwrite-service v2.3 -> canary pool at 02:50 UTC.

Arjun: write amplification? dual-write doubles inserts; need to ensure WAL throughput and IO headroom.

Maria: dry-run shows ~1.9x WAL increase due to compression. We have headroom but will throttle backfill. Proposed knobs: concurrency=8, batch_size=5000, sleep_ms=200.

Sam: can you paste the backfill SQL for explain on staging?

Maria: simplified backfill SQL:
```
INSERT INTO route_key_v2 (tenant_id, v2_key, created_at)
SELECT tenant_id, fn_generate_v2(route_key_v1), now()
FROM route_key_v1
WHERE tenant_id = ANY($1::bigint[])
ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, v2_key) DO NOTHING;
```

Devon: add a shadow-verify step to compare per-tenant counts between v1 and v2 and emit backfill.count_mismatch{tenant_id}.

Lee: rollback plan?

Maria: short: stop backfill, flip proxy to v1-only flag, delete recent alias rows if we need a fast revert. full rollback runbook is in drive: /eng/platform/migrations/tenant-reshard-rollback.md

Arjun: alerts to wire before starting:
- alias_cardinality > baseline * 1.25
- backfill.rate < configured threshold for 5m
- console-read-shard.p99_latency > 2.5s
- backfill.count_mismatch_rate > 0.5% across canary tenants

Sam: who is on triage during the backfill window?

Maria: oncall: @devon, db backup oncall: @arjun, ops support: @lee. Join #release-war-room at 02:45 UTC.

Devon: i'll own canary rollout and dashboard monitoring. will post a short runbook and a checklist in the channel before 02:30.

Maria: final checklist in thread: dual-write deployed to canary, alias-table migration applied, read-adapter flag staged, backfill scheduled, alerts wired. if no objections we start.

Lee: +1

Arjun: +1, DB metrics look ok.

Sam: +1 LGTM.

Maria: kicking off canary at 02:50 UTC. will post updates here.

Console-bot: canary started: dualwrite-service/v2.3 on canary pool (id: canary-11)

Maria: canary after 30m: alias_cardinality +3%, console p99_read_latency +0.15s, backfill.count_mismatch 0.12% — ramping to 10% steady.

Devon: noticed a UI glitch on one dashboard panel, filed ENG-4421. pausing ramp 15m to investigate.

Maria: pausing ramp and investigating. will post remediation steps in 10m.
